resale_co.name: Occupancy Transfer Certificate (Occupancy Transfer Inspection)
resale_co.issued_by: Egg Harbor City Code Enforcement Officer (applications go to the City Construction Office / Building Department)
requirements: Occupancy transfer certificate needed before a dwelling is sold, transferred or rented (City Code Section 213-6H, PM-107.6)

Inspection covers cleanliness, walls and ceilings, doors and hardware, windows, storm windows and screens, exterior paint and maintenance, a visual roof check, basement, kitchen, bathrooms, smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detector, electrical outlets, switches, covers and fuse box cover, sidewalks, lawn, shrubs and trees, maximum bedroom occupancy and all City code, zoning and planning ordinances
Submit the Smoke and Carbon Monoxide Alarm Certificate Application together with the Occupancy Transfer Inspection form
Form asks for owner, purchaser, tenant and lock box details and the building type, bedrooms, heat, sewer/septic and water/well

fees.label: Occupancy transfer certificate inspection, per dwelling unit (covers the first inspection and one follow-up)
fees.quote: A nonrefundable inspection fee of $75 for each dwelling unit shall be paid to the City of Egg Harbor at the time of application for such occupancy transfer certificate.

fees.label: Each additional inspection after one follow-up
fees.quote: In the event more than on follow-up inspection is needed, there shall be an additional charge of $25 for each additional inspection.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Download the Occupancy Transfer Inspection Form from Forms & Documents, mark it SALE, and submit it with the Smoke and Carbon Monoxide Alarm Certificate Application to the Egg Harbor City Construction Office, 500 London Ave., Egg Harbor City, NJ 08215 ($75.00 per unit). Pay with exact cash, money order or check made out to City of Egg Harbor City, or online through the City's WIPP portal (2.95% fee).
resale_co.contact_title: Land Use and Building Department Office Manager

evidence.quote: No owner or leaseholder or his agent shall rent, sell, transfer, grant, lease, let, mortgage with right of occupancy or otherwise dispose of the ownership or occupancy

unless an occupancy transfer certificate, certifying that the building and premises are in compliance with the Code and all other ordinances of the City of Egg Harbor City, shall first be obtained from the Code Enforcement Officer of the City.
Any property owner that fails to obtain an occupancy transfer certificate required as outlined above shall be subject to a fine of $150.
$75 for sale or rental including fire certification and one follow-up. 3rd inspection is $25

resale_co.notes: The City code (Section 213-6H, PM-107.6 Occupancy Transfer Certificate, now readable in full on ecode360) bars selling or transferring any dwelling without an occupancy transfer certificate from the Code Enforcement Officer, charges $75 per dwelling unit for the first inspection and one follow-up, $25 for each inspection after that, and a $150 fine for skipping it. The City fee table (Section 120-2A, last amended by Ord. No. 13-2025 on 9-11-2025) and the August 2025 Schedule A list the same $75 'for sale or rental including fire certification and one follow-up', yet the City's April 2026 smoke/CO application charges its own $55/$90/$160 fees, so ask whether both are paid. The $25 extra-inspection fee, listed as an open question last time, is now confirmed from the code text. The City's document links (app.membershipware.com viewBlob) changed behaviour since the last check: they now answer with a redirect to a viewer page on eggharborcity.org, so a normal browser may land on the City home page instead of the PDF; the PDF bytes are still sent along with the redirect and were read in full on 2026-10-06, so the form quotes (Occupancy Transfer Inspection form and smoke/CO application) are confirmed by hand but an automatic check that follows the redirect will not find them. The redirect target is https://www.eggharborcity.org/index?i=<document id>&rf=i. The Forms & Documents page is built by script, so its document descriptions are cited from the City's forms data feed (app.membershipware.com mwjsResources). Code Enforcement Officer: Robert McClain (codeenforcement2@eggharborcity.org). The City also schedules annual rental unit inspections (rental program).

requirements: 10-year sealed battery smoke alarm in every bedroom (depending on construction year)
Basement smoke alarm at the bottom of the stairwell at ceiling level (not between joists)
Hallway smoke alarms within 10 feet of all bedroom doors
Electric smoke alarms required by the building code cannot be replaced with battery alarms
Smoke detectors at least 3 feet from ceiling fan blade tips and air ducts; none in kitchens, bathrooms, dead air space, crawl spaces or attics
CO alarm in the hallway within 10 feet of all bedrooms; not plugged into a switched outlet
Fire extinguisher: residential 2A:10B:C, no larger than 10 lb, mounted within 10 feet of the kitchen (form still lists it)

authorities.name: Egg Harbor City Fire Official (Fire Marshal), Fire Prevention
authorities.lead_time: Fee depends on how many days before the Certificate of Occupancy must be issued: more than 10 days, 4 to 10 days, or fewer than 4 days. Inspections are available Tuesdays and Thursdays from 2 to 6 pm.

fees.label: Smoke/CO inspection, requested more than 10 days before the certificate is needed (per unit)
fees.quote: Initial inspections requested more than 10 days before the Certificate of Occupancy must be issued: $55 per unit.

fees.label: Smoke/CO inspection, requested 4 to 10 days before the certificate is needed (per unit)
fees.quote: Initial inspections requested between 4 and 10 days before the Certificate of Occupancy must be issued: $90 per unit.

fees.label: Smoke/CO inspection, requested fewer than 4 days before the certificate is needed (per unit)
fees.quote: Initial inspections requested fewer than 4 days before the Certificate of Occupancy must be issued: $160 per unit.

fees.label: First reinspection when more than one follow-up inspection is needed
fees.quote: In the event more than one follow-up inspection is needed, there shall be an additional charge of $50 for the first reinspection.

authorities.how_to_apply: Fill out the Smoke and Carbon Monoxide Alarm Certificate Application (Forms & Documents) and submit it with the Occupancy Transfer Inspection form to the City, 500 London Ave., Egg Harbor City, NJ 08215. Questions: EHCFirePrevention@eggharborcity.org. After a failed reinspection the process starts over with a new fee.
authorities.contact_title: Fire Marshal (also Construction Official and Electric, Plumbing, Fire & Mechanical Subcode Official)

fire_cert.notes: Egg Harbor City's fire code enforcing agency is its fire department (registry code F); the Fire Official, Stephen Buchhofer, is also the City's Construction Official. The office number recorded is City Hall's line, (609) 965-0081, which the state directory lists under smoke detector compliance; the directory's 856 number and non-City email for the fire official are not recorded. Fees come from the City's April 2026 smoke/CO application (re-read 2026-10-06). Its link now redirects to a City viewer page (see resale notes), so the fee quotes may not show up for an automatic check even though the PDF text is unchanged. The form still lists a fire extinguisher even though P.L.2025, c.19 (February 3, 2025) removed it from the state requirement. The City fee table says the $75 occupancy transfer fee includes fire certification, which does not match the separate smoke/CO fees on this form.

open_questions: Does the $75 occupancy transfer fee cover the smoke/CO certificate (the City fee table says 'including fire certification'), or are the $55/$90/$160 smoke/CO fees on the April 2026 form charged on top?
How far ahead to apply for the occupancy transfer inspection and how long the certificate stays valid (not published).
Does the City still require a portable fire extinguisher at resale after P.L.2025, c.19?
